AcmeApp (customer): hey team — over the last ~18h we've had our p99 token latency for requests to model `gptx-extended-v1` jump from ~420ms to ~1.3s. p95 up too. No config changes on our side. This started right after the new model was onboarded. Can you help? :grimacing:
Maya (support): sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a few example requests (headers redacted) and approximate seq lengths?
AcmeApp (customer): sure. most calls are chat completions with ~12 messages, prompt tokens ~1.2k, completion target ~512. here's a curl we use (safe to share):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -d '{"model":"gptx-extended-v1","input":"<long chat>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
AcmeApp (customer): latency graph — p99 sits at 1.25s since 2026-02-13T03:00Z, before that ~420ms. Error rate is unchanged.
Maya (support): thanks. routing you to oncall eng-sre — @Raj can you take a look?
Raj (eng-sre): looking. can you share a sample response header (x-model-variant, x-route-id, x-kv-cache-hit)? do you see any 503s/timeouts?
AcmeApp (customer): 0 503s. sample headers: x-model-variant: gptx-extended-v1-quant, x-route-id: region-eu-3, x-kv-cache-hit: false (mostly).
Raj (eng-sre): interesting — kv cache misses for long-context workloads would increase compute. @Liam any topology/serve changes in eu-3 around that time?
Liam (eng-runtime): we rolled a tokenizer patch during the onboarding — switched to new BPE merges for that model to reduce token counts for multi-lingual inputs. That patch changed tokenization boundaries subtly. Could that increase tokenized length for these prompts?
Olivia (eng-ml): yes, tokenizer changes can go either way. in our internal perf tests we saw nominal token count reductions on average, but some long conversational english sequences regressed because of merge ordering. if tokenized input increased, KV cache alignment can break and prefix cache reuse drops.
Raj (eng-sre): do we have traces for those requests? @Liam can you pull a trace for a 1.3s p99 request from region-eu-3 — we need span breakdown (tokenization, kv-restore, decode loop).
Liam (eng-runtime): pulling traces now...
DeployBot: canary rollout gptx-extended-v1-tokenizer-v2 -> region-eu-3 started by Olivia at 2026-02-13T02:45Z
Liam (eng-runtime): traces show tokenization step jumped from ~18ms -> ~110ms; kv-restore time unchanged but kv cache hit drops from ~82% -> ~6% for these requests. total GPU decode time per request increased because sequence length after tokenization is +18% in bad cases.
Olivia (eng-ml): that aligns — tokenizer-v2 produces more tokens for certain long-turn dialogues, especially where there are repeated whitespace/newline patterns and non-ascii chars. more tokens => longer attention compute and larger KV entries => cache alignment issues.
Maya (support): customer impact summary for AcmeApp: p99 grows from 420ms to 1.3s, p95 from 240ms -> ~680ms, no errors but user-perceived slowness. Recommended short term mitigations?
Raj (eng-sre): short-term: route this customer's traffic (and other affected routes in region-eu-3) to a stable model variant (gptx-extended-v1-tokenizer-v1) while we investigate. also disable canary for tokenizer-v2 in eu-3 to stop further exposure.
Liam (eng-runtime): agreed — can add a routing rule for their route id (region-eu-3/acme-route) to map to tokenizer-v1 variant. will do a quick canary rollback.
DeployBot: rollback initiated: gptx-extended-v1-tokenizer-v2 -> rollback to tokenizer-v1 in region-eu-3 by Liam at 2026-02-13T03:05Z
Liam (eng-runtime): rollback done. I've pinned acme-route to tokenizer-v1 for 24h. can you confirm p99 back to baseline?
AcmeApp (customer): rerunning tests now... refreshing graphs... p99 down to 430ms. p95 260ms. looks like it's back. thanks.
Olivia (eng-ml): long-term: we need to expand our tokenizer perf matrix to include long multi-turn dialogue fixtures from customers (non-ascii, repeated newlines, system messages) and add automated token-count distribution alerts during canaries. Also add a KV-cache-impact simulation: compute tokenized length delta and expected kv-entry-size change to flag regressions before rollout.
Raj (eng-sre): operational controls: require a pre-rollout perf gate for tokenizer changes: run canary traffic against live-like route ids with representative context lengths, and fail canary if p99 increases > 20% or kv-hit drops > 30%.
Maya (support): next steps for AcmeApp — sorry again, we'll keep you updated. we'll leave routing pinned for 24h and then slowly unpin after we expand canary tests. any docs or checklist you want me to share with the customer?
Olivia (eng-ml): please share a short note: root cause = tokenizer-v2 increased tokenization length for some long-turn dialogues leading to higher compute and KV cache miss rates. mitigation = rollback to tokenizer-v1. committed follow-ups: expand canary fixtures, add perf gates, and add tokenization delta alerts.
Maya (support): sending note now.
Maya (support): NOTE TO SELF / ENG: create a runbook entry for tokenizer canary failures and add a monitoring alert for token_count_distribution shifts during canary (link to internal ticket created: INF-7823).
Raj (eng-sre): filing incident follow-up and retrospective items. tagging @Olivia @Liam.
Olivia (eng-ml): I'll open a model-onboarding checklist PR with added tokenization perf tests (PR: ml/tokenizer-canary-gates).
Liam (eng-runtime): adding runtime flag to simulate kv-hit drop locally for faster repro (branch: runtime/kv-sim).
AcmeApp (customer): appreciate the quick response. we rely on low tail latency. please ping when canary tests are in place and when it's safe to try tokenizer-v2 again.
Maya (support): will do — closing loop once follow-ups merged. :thumbsup:
